assets.description: Optional per-image-key metadata from pick_asset: field key → {alt?: string, srcset?: object {"<width>": "<url>"} exactly as pick_asset returned it, mobile?}. Only for keys whose value is an image URL.

target.description: What is edited: a section on a page, the merged global settings, the branding slice, or a page's own options.

kind.description: section = one section row on a page; global = site-wide settings (header, footer, product cards, typography, Branding panel BrandingSection: store name, logo, favicon…); branding = ONLY age gate, location picker, certifications; page = a page's own options (plus "published"). page.description: Page slug for kind section|page. Omit to act on the page the merchant is currently viewing (the host fills it in); pass one only when the merchant names a different page. Manifest pages: account, age-gate, blog, blog-detail, cart, checkout, faq, home, location-selection, login, order-confirmation, order-details, privacy-policy, product-details, products, return-refund, seo, terms-of-service; custom pages use their slug from the context.

panel.description: kind global, optional: narrow to one panel (BrandingSection, ButtonsSection, FooterSection, HeaderSection, InsiderBannerSection, LayoutSection, NotificationSection, ProductCardSection, ShopMenuSection, SidebarCartSection, SocialMediaSection, TypographyColorsSection). sectionId.description: kind section: the section's id exactly as listed in the turn context sections (e.g. heroBanner, productCarousel-2, contentBlock-3), or the page's built-in __pinned_* id to edit a built-in block's options.

storeId.description: kind section on the location-details page only: the location id whose per-store section list is edited. Omit everywhere else.

values.description: Field key → new value. Use null to clear a field (writes its unset_value).

name: set_fields
description: Write one or more fields on a target. Keys are manifest field keys (never storage paths); values are typed per the field (color hex, number, bool, enum member, text/richtext HTML, image = CDN token or absolute URL, null = clear). Call lookup_fields first for any key you have not confirmed in this conversation; never invent keys. Dotted keys address keyed fields (locationOverrides.<locId>.<f>, categories.<slug>.<f>) and SEO keys (pages.<page>.title). On hero sections the flat keys mirror slides[0] — prefer edit_list update on slides index 0. After pick_asset put the returned public_url in values and its alt/srcset in assets under the same key — srcset is an OBJECT {"<width>": "<url>"} and must be copied exactly as returned, never rewritten as a string. Fields flagged ro (derived) are read-only (E_READONLY).

action.description: add | remove | reorder | update | duplicate. `update` is allowed on every list; `duplicate` only on a page's sections list.

index.description: Row index (0-based) for remove/update/duplicate, or the parent index for add on a nested list. Nested lists take [parentIdx, childIdx].

item.description: add: the new row's fields (missing keys take the list's defaults). update: only the fields to change — the row's other fields are kept.

list.description: The list key on the target (e.g. slides, slides[].bullets, reviews, faqCategories[].items, sections).

order.description: reorder only: the COMPLETE new order — list EVERY current row exactly once (a 3-row list needs 3 entries; to move one row, write the full new order, e.g. [1, 0, 2] — a partial order such as [1, 0] is refused, E_ORDER). Plain lists take 0-based indexes into the current rows. ID-KEYED lists take the row ids, NEVER indexes: a list that describe_target / lookup_fields shows with `orders` (filterOrder, headerNavOrder, footerNavOrder, paymentMethodsOrder, cardChipOrder, sortOptionsOrder, …) e.g. ["brand", "category", "price", …] with every current id, and a page's sections list (section ids). An E_ORDER reply names the valid ids / the row count: resend the full order.

sectionId.description: sections list only: address the row by its id instead of index (remove/update/duplicate).

name: edit_list
description: Edit one list on a target: add a row, remove / duplicate a row, reorder rows, or update one row's fields (how detail panels — reviews, FAQ items, hero bullets, posts, footer columns — are edited). ONE structural change (add/remove/reorder/duplicate) per call; `reorder` writes the COMPLETE new order (see `order`). Nested lists use the dotted key (slides[].bullets) and an index array [parentIdx, childIdx]; `add` on a nested list takes the parent index only. On a page target the list "sections" is the page's own section rows {id,type,enabled}: add takes item {id: <sectionType>} (the item's id IS the section type to add; the host assigns the row's instance id), update only {enabled}, duplicate copies a row, and built-in __pinned_* rows cannot be added, removed or reordered (E_PINNED). Lists and their allowed ops come from describe_target or lookup_fields {list}. Known lists — sections.blog: pageVisibility.blog.posts; sections.blogSection: pageVisibility.blog.posts; sections.contentBlock: bullets, faqs, images, imagesAlt, imagesLink, items, milestones, tiers; sections.featuredCategories: pageVisibility.products.categoryOrder; sections.gallery: images; sections.hero: slides, slides[].bullets; sections.heroBanner: slides, slides[].bullets; sections.locations: disabledLocationIds, locationOrder; sections.loyaltyForm: infoSections; sections.milestones: faqs, milestones; sections.perksCards: bullets, faqs, images, imagesAlt, imagesLink, imagesSrcSet, items, milestones, tiers; sections.perksIcons: bullets, faqs, images, imagesAlt, imagesLink, imagesSrcSet, items, milestones, tiers; sections.promotion: items, weekdayItems; sections.reviews: reviews; sections.testimonials: reviews; globalPanels.FooterSection: footerCustomColumns, footerCustomColumns[].links, footerLocationOrder, pageVisibility._meta.footerBottomCustomLinks, pageVisibility._meta.footerBottomOrder, pageVisibility._meta.footerNavCustomLinks, pageVisibility._meta.footerNavOrder, paymentMethodsOrder; globalPanels.HeaderSection: pageVisibility._meta.headerNavCustomLinks, pageVisibility._meta.headerNavOrder; globalPanels.ProductCardSection: cardChipOrder, cardRibbonColorRules; globalPanels.ShopMenuSection: shopMenuItems; branding: certifications; pages.blog: posts; pages.blog-detail: blog.posts; pages.faq: faqCategories, faqCategories[].items; pages.privacy-policy: privacyContent; pages.product-details: productDetail.chipOrder; pages.products: filterOrder, productListCategoryOrder, sortOptionsOrder; pages.return-refund: returnRefundContent; pages.terms-of-service: termsContent; details.CategoryDetailsPanel: childCategoryOrder. Section types for sections.add: blog, blogSection, content, contentBlock, featuredCategories, gallery, hero, heroBanner, locations, loyaltyForm, milestones, newsletter, perksCards, perksIcons, productCarousel, promotion, reviews, sectionDivider, testimonials.

name: reset
description: Clear SPECIFIC fields back to their unset state (the editor's ↺ button): exactly the keys you list are written as their manifest unset_value — nothing else on the target changes, and NOT the template default (use restore_default for that). Clearing a whole target (every field of a section, page or panel) is not available: list every key you mean, confirmed via lookup_fields, one call per target. A call without keys is refused (E_OP) and nothing is cleared.

keys.description: The field keys to restore — only these are touched. At least one; every key must be a field of the target (dotted keyed keys allowed).

name: restore_default
description: Put SPECIFIC fields back to the template's default value (the manifest `default`), going through the normal write path (companions, mirror, aliases): exactly the keys you list are restored — nothing else on the target changes. A listed key with no default is cleared to its unset_value instead. Restoring a whole target (every field of a section, page or panel) is not available: list every key you mean, confirmed via lookup_fields. A call without keys is refused (E_OP) and nothing is restored.

layout.description: The layout id for that page (e.g. filter-left, tab, summary-left, accordion, hero-featured).

page.description: Page slug. Omit for the page the merchant is viewing. Pages: home, account, age-gate, blog, blog-detail, cart, checkout, faq, home, location-selection, login, order-confirmation, order-details, privacy-policy, product-details, products, return-refund, seo, terms-of-service.

name: set_page_layout
description: Switch a page's layout preset (a different setting from per-page options). Layout ids per page come from the turn context (context.layout is the current one; the host rejects unknown ids and returns the valid ones). Changing the HOME layout also re-seeds the home sections to the preset — say so before doing it.

in_nav.description: Optional: true also adds the page to the header menu. Only when the merchant asks for it; otherwise omit.

slug.description: Optional: the page's path segment, only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (e.g. "summer-events"); anything else is refused. Omit to derive it from the title; pass it when a later call in the same batch targets the new page.

status.description: Optional: published (default) = served at /<slug> once saved; draft = saved but not served, and hidden from the editor's page list. Use draft only when the merchant asks for it.

title.description: The new page's name as the merchant gave it, plain text, at most 80 characters (e.g. "Deals", "Summer Events").

name: create_page
description: Create ONE new, empty custom page in the editor's unsaved draft (what the Pages tab's "New page" does). It goes live at /<slug> only when the merchant presses Save and Publish, and it is in the header menu only with in_nav true. The result returns the page's final `slug`: then target the new page with {"kind":"page","page":<slug>} (edit_list on its list "sections" to add sections) or {"kind":"section","page":<slug>,…}. To add sections in the SAME batch as the create, pass `slug` yourself and use exactly that slug; if the create is refused, those later calls are refused too. Refused, with nothing created, when the title or slug matches a page that already exists (edit that page instead), when the slug is reserved or not already lowercase words joined by hyphens, or on a template that cannot show custom pages; the error says which and may suggest a free slug. Renaming, duplicating or deleting pages is not available (report_unsupported where pages).

page.description: The page whose built-in block is reset.

sectionId.description: The page's pinned id (must belong to that page).

name: reset_pinned_section
description: Reset a page's built-in (pinned) block to its template defaults: re-enables it and clears any stored settings for it. Built-in blocks (FAQ, product list, cart, checkout, legal pages…) can only be reset — never added, removed, reordered or disabled.

purpose.description: One short sentence shown to the merchant: what the image is for (e.g. "Hero banner background").

name: pick_asset
description: Ask the merchant to pick an image from their asset library. Call it ALONE (no other tool calls in the same response) and stop; the turn resumes with the picked asset {public_url, alt?, srcset?} as this call's result, where srcset is an object {"<width>": "<url>"}. Then write the URL with set_fields (values) and its alt/srcset (assets — copy the srcset object as-is). Never invent image URLs.

container.description: Instead of target: a manifest container path (globalPanels = every panel merged).

help.description: Include each field's help text (longer output).

keys.description: Exact field keys to describe (mirror aliases such as ctaText and keyed keys such as locationOverrides.<locId>.address resolve too).

list.description: Only this list's row fields (e.g. slides, reviews, faqCategories[].items, sections).

query.description: Case-insensitive match on key prefix, camelCase word, label text or list key, e.g. "headline", "color", "button".

name: lookup_fields
description: Look up the editable fields of a target (or a manifest container) before writing: returns each matching field's key, type, label, enum (+labels), min/max/step, default, unset_value, gates (if/hide), ro (derived, read-only), ref, keyed_by, companions, the list it belongs to and its panel; plus the container's lists. A field's panel is a global panel name you may pass as target.panel, EXCEPT a details panel (…DetailsPanel, …DetailPanel): that is where the editor shows a list row or keyed key, never a target panel — write it with edit_list update on its list, or set_fields with the dotted key on its own target. Narrow with query (key prefix, camelCase word, label substring or list key), keys (exact keys, aliases and dotted keyed keys included) or list (that list's row fields). Compact and capped — refine rather than paginate.

name: describe_target
description: Describe a target (or container): its lists with allowed ops / orders / detail panel, its field key stems (or every key when few), the hero mirror, presets, keyed-key prefixes and — for a page — its built-in pinned section id. Cheap orientation before lookup_fields.

manual_hint.description: Optional: where in the editor the merchant could do it themselves, if you know.

reason.description: Plain-language reason, one or two sentences, merchant-facing.

where.description: Optional: where the merchant makes this change — the place system rules name for each value ("What Sous Chef cannot change"). The browser shows a link there. Use "support" when no other value fits.

name: report_unsupported
description: Tell the merchant a request cannot be done by editing this site's configuration (no matching field or list after looking it up, or something outside the editor). Use it instead of guessing a key, never together with an edit. Set `where` to the place the change is made; the UI shows the reason with a link there. Then say in one sentence where they can do it. Never fabricate an email address or claim to have sent anything.
